subtitle: A Vakataka Minister, a Buddhist Cave, and a Mountain of Merit

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of the cliff face of Ajanta with Cave 16 looming, river and jungle below
panels.action: Varahadeva stands at the edge of the newly carved terrace of Cave 16, robes stirring in the gorge wind, the dark square mouth of the vihara behind him and the sheer rock wall towering above.

dialogue.text: In Harishena’s age, a Shaiva-Vaishnava minister carved a Buddhist monastery into living rock—leaving, in one prasasti, the richest voice of the Vakatakas.

i18n.hi: हरीशेन के समय का एक शैव–वैष्णव मंत्री, जीवित शिला में बौद्ध विहार गढ़ गया—और एक ही प्रशस्ति में वाकाटकों की सबसे गूंजती आवाज छोड़ गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high aerial view down into the Waghora gorge
panels.action: From high above, the Waghora river curls through a horseshoe of cliffs; tiny anthill-like workers cling to the rock where Cave 16 will be, while Varahadeva watches from a ledge, a small figure against the stone.

dialogue.text: On a remote bend of the Waghora, stone rang with hammer blows. Here, at Ajanta, a minister of the Vakatakas chose to inscribe his world into a mountain.

i18n.hi: दूर, वाघोरा की मोड़ पर, पत्थर हथौड़ों से गूंज उठा। यहीं अजंता में, वाकाटक मंत्री ने अपना युग पहाड़ पर खुदवा दिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Varahadeva in court robes, half in shadow, with hints of a palace behind
panels.action: Varahadeva stands in an interior hall, wearing elegant court garments and a simple sacred thread, his face thoughtful, pillars and faint mural patterns suggesting a Vakataka palace.

dialogue.text: Varahadeva was no monk. He was a courtier, a brahman, a servant of Harishena—the last great king of the Vakatakas, whose banners spread across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: वराहदेव कोई भिक्षु नहीं था। वह दरबारी था, ब्राह्मण था, हरीशेन का सेवक—वाकाटकों का अंतिम महान नरेश, जिसके ध्वज पूरे दक्खिन में फहरा उठे।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot of Varahadeva before a shrine with a Vishnu Varaha image
panels.action: In a private shrine, Varahadeva offers flowers at the feet of a stone Varaha, the boar incarnation of Vishnu; oil lamps glow, smoke curling toward the ceiling.

dialogue.text: His very name, Varahadeva, tied him to Vishnu’s boar avatar. The prasasti calls him devoted to the feet of the gods—yet his great gift was to the Buddha’s community.

i18n.hi: उसका नाम ही, वराहदेव, उसे विष्णु के वराह अवतार से जोड़ता था। प्रशस्ति कहती है, वह देवों के चरणों का दास था—फिर भी उसका बड़ा दान बुद्ध-समुदाय को गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ajanta cliff with multiple cave facades, workers and monks moving about
panels.action: The cliff is dotted with cave façades in various stages of carving; artisans chip rock, monks in simple robes walk the ledges, and Varahadeva stands conferring with a senior monk near the future Cave 16.

dialogue.text: At Ajanta, kings, princes and officials competed in devotion. Each cut rock, raised pillars, painted walls—offering monasteries to the sangha as lasting stores of merit.

i18n.hi: अजंता में राजा, कुमार और अमात्य भक्ति में होड़ करते थे। हर कोई चट्टान काटता, स्तंभ उठाता, भित्ति रचता—संगह को विहार समर्पित कर स्थायी पुण्य-भंडार बनाता।

panels.shot: intimate medium two-shot of Varahadeva and an unnamed elder monk, seen from behind Varahadeva
panels.action: From behind Varahadeva’s shoulder, we see an elder monk gesturing toward the blank cliff face, palms joined, while Varahadeva listens, his hand resting on a rolled plan or palm-leaf bundle.

dialogue.speaker: Varahadeva
dialogue.text: Let this rock shelter your community long after my bones are dust.

i18n.hi: यह शिला तुम्हारे समुदाय को तब तक संभाले, जब तक मेरी हड्डियाँ भी मिट्टी न हो जाएँ।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of workers carving inward into the cliff, lit by torches
panels.action: Inside the half-carved hall, laborers strike chisels into the living rock, dust hanging in shafts of torchlight as Varahadeva walks along the rough floor, inspecting the emerging columns.

dialogue.text: Cave 16 did not grow upward like a temple. It receded, hollowed day by day, a mountain turned inside out by men who believed stone could be shaped into piety.

i18n.hi: गुफा १६ मंदिर की तरह ऊपर नहीं बढ़ी। वह भीतर जाती गई, रोज़ रोज़ खोदी गई, पर्वत को उलट दिया उन लोगों ने, जो मानते थे कि पत्थर को आस्था का रूप दिया जा सकता है।

panels.shot: medium wide of painters on scaffolds working on a wall panel, with Varahadeva below
panels.action: Painters stand on wooden scaffolds inside the finished hall, laying pigments on a large wall scene, while below Varahadeva watches, hands clasped, his face lit by the wet colors.

dialogue.text: When the rock was tamed, color followed. Stories of the Buddha’s lives, lay donors, princes and queens—Varahadeva’s cave became a painted scripture.

i18n.hi: जब चट्टान वश में आई, रंग चले। बुद्ध के जीवनों की कथाएँ, दानी गृहस्थ, राजकुमार और रानियाँ—वराहदेव की गुफा चित्रित धर्म-पुस्तक बन गई।

panels.shot: closer shot of the famous Dying Princess painting, with Varahadeva small in the corner observing
panels.action: The ‘Dying Princess’ scene fills most of the frame: a frail princess reclines, attendants clustered around; in the shadowed corner, Varahadeva stands respectfully, head slightly bowed toward the scene.

dialogue.text: Among these scenes, later eyes would name one the ‘Dying Princess’—a human moment of illness and care, preserved under the minister’s patronage in flickering tempera on rock.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं दृश्यों में बाद की आँखों ने एक को ‘मरणासन्न राजकुमारी’ कहा—बीमारी और सेवा का मानवीय क्षण, मंत्री के संरक्षण में, झिलमिलाते रंगों में पत्थर पर थमा हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot of a stone pillar base where an artisan carves inscription lines, Varahadeva nearby
panels.action: An artisan crouches at the base of a pillar near the entrance, carefully incising neat lines of Brahmi script; Varahadeva stands over him, holding a palm-leaf manuscript, dictating.

dialogue.text: But his true voice lay not in paint. On the right wall of the entrance, he ordered a long prasasti carved—a tide of Sanskrit that praised gods, family, king and cave.

i18n.hi: पर उसकी असली आवाज रंग में नहीं थी। प्रवेश-द्वार की दाहिनी दीवार पर उसने एक लम्बी प्रशस्ति खुदवायी—संस्कृत की लहर, जो देव, कुल, नरेश और गुफा सबको गाती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the inscription lines, shallow depth of field; Varahadeva’s hand enters frame
panels.action: The frame focuses tightly on crisp, newly carved characters on the stone; Varahadeva’s hand rests lightly beside them, fingertips dusty, as if feeling the permanence of the words.

dialogue.text: In it, he names his brahman lineage, their learning, their devotion. He traces the Vakataka genealogy, sets Harishena in that line, and binds himself to their story in stone.

i18n.hi: उसमें वह अपने ब्राह्मण कुल का नाम लेता है, उनका ज्ञान, उनकी भक्ति गिनाता है। वह वाकाटक वंश की कड़ी जोड़ता है, उस धारा में हरीशेन को बैठा कर खुद को उनकी शिला-गाथा से बाँध देता है।

panels.shot: wide imaginative shot of a royal army on the march superimposed as a faint vignette over Varahadeva reading
panels.action: Varahadeva stands reading a palm-leaf draft; around him, faint, almost transparent images of marching soldiers and elephants evoke the conquests he praises, without dominating the scene.

dialogue.text: The prasasti speaks of Harishena’s victories, of lands brought under his umbrella. Modern scholars read these as eulogy more than report—but they reveal what a minister wanted remembered.

i18n.hi: प्रशस्ति हरीशेन की विजयों का गुणगान करती है, उन देशों का जो उसके छत्र के नीचे आए। आज के विद्वान इन्हें वर्णन से ज्यादा स्तुति मानते हैं—पर इससे पता चलता है मंत्री क्या याद रखवाना चाहता था।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Varahadeva before a seated Buddha image, monks around, with the inscription wall visible behind
panels.action: Within the cave, Varahadeva stands with joined palms before a serene seated Buddha; behind him, monks sit in quiet rows, and on the side wall the faint carved lines of the inscription can be seen.

dialogue.text: He dedicates the vihara to the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha—yet his devotion to Hindu deities is also proclaimed. At Ajanta, such layered piety was not a contradiction, but a norm.

i18n.hi: वह यह विहार बुद्ध, धर्म और संघ को समर्पित करता है—पर अपने हिंदू देवताओं की भक्ति भी खुलकर लिखवाता है। अजंता में ऐसी तहदार श्रद्धा विरोध नहीं, सामान्य बात थी।

panels.shot: close-up on Varahadeva’s face in half-light, eyes lowered, as if silently reciting his own inscription
panels.action: Varahadeva’s face fills the frame, lit from one side by lamplight; his lips are slightly parted, eyes lowered in introspective calm, the suggestion of carved letters blurred in the background.

dialogue.text: He calls his cave a ‘mountain of merit’ for his parents, his king, himself. A minister’s loyalty becomes a spiritual economy: political service converted into karmic credit.

i18n.hi: वह अपनी गुफा को माता-पिता, स्वामी और अपने लिए ‘पुण्य का पर्वत’ कहता है। मंत्री की निष्ठा आध्यात्मिक लेन-देन बन जाती है: राज-सेवा कर्म का खाता भरने लगती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a later, emptier Ajanta hall, paint faded, with Varahadeva imagined as a ghostlike figure
panels.action: Centuries later, the same hall appears dim and neglected, paint flaking, bat silhouettes faint; an almost transparent Varahadeva stands where he once did, the rock unchanged around him.

dialogue.text: Ajanta would fall silent. Monks depart, paint fades, jungle presses in. Yet the inscription survives storms and centuries, whispering the minister’s carefully chosen words to any who can still read them.

i18n.hi: अजंता मौन हो गई। भिक्षु चले गए, रंग फीके पड़े, जंगल ने घेर लिया। फिर भी यह लेख आँधियों और सदियों से बचा, मंत्री के तौले हुए शब्द आज भी किसी पढ़ने वाले से फुसफुसाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern scholar’s hand tracing the inscription, with an imagined Varahadeva mirrored on the stone
panels.action: A modern, anonymous hand with a notebook gently traces the carved letters; in the polished sheen of the stone, an imagined reflection of Varahadeva appears, as if the past watches the present.

dialogue.text: Today, historians lean close, copying each line. Through this single prasasti, they reconstruct Harishena’s reach, Varahadeva’s family, the web of beliefs that met in this carved corridor.

i18n.hi: आज इतिहासकार झुककर हर पंक्ति नकल करते हैं। इस एक प्रशस्ति से वे हरीशेन की पहुँच, वराहदेव का कुल, और उन आस्थाओं का जाल जोड़ते हैं जो इस तराशी हुई गलियारे में मिली थीं।

panels.shot: final sweeping wide of Cave 16 façade at sunrise, tiny figures of visitors at the steps
panels.action: At sunrise, the façade of Cave 16 glows golden; small modern visitors ascend the steps, while Varahadeva is envisioned standing at the threshold, hands folded toward the hall within and the valley beyond.

dialogue.text: Varahadeva’s mountain of merit shows how power, faith and art once met in a single act of giving—and how a minister’s carefully carved praise can outlast his king, his dynasty, and his world.

i18n.hi: वराहदेव का पुण्य-पर्वत दिखाता है कैसे कभी शक्ति, आस्था और कला एक ही दान में मिल गए—और कैसे एक मंत्री की तराशी हुई स्तुति उसके राजा, उसके वंश, और उसकी दुनिया से भी अधिक टिक गई।

title_i18n.en: Varahadeva Carves a Mountain of Merit

subtitle_i18n.en: A Vakataka Minister, a Buddhist Cave, and a Mountain of Merit
subtitle_i18n.hi: वाकाटक मंत्री, बौद्ध गुफा, और पुण्य का पहाड़
